subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, skipped, queued, or remain parallel by default, and should any 409 behavior be opt-in?
rationale: The requested 409 changes an external webhook HTTP response contract and retry semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the default, compatibility, or security posture without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior, then let trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

options.title: Make 409 The Default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default and accept that existing webhook integrations may need migration to avoid retry storms.

options.title: Keep Caller-Managed Locking
options.body: Leave OpenClaw accepting hook deliveries and document idempotency keys plus client-side locks as the supported overlap control.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Overlap Policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior, then let trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest prior policy framing for this hook/session admission decision and relevant hook security history.
